1. (Currently amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
a ring oscillator configured to generate a plurality of independent first entropy values;
a mixing circuit configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function or hash function to generate a second entropy value;
a pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value and configured to generate a random number; and
a cryptographic circuit configured to produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number, wherein the system is further configured to implement __countermeasures against phase tracking attacks on the ring oscillator-based entropy source by__ [[receive a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source; apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value; seed a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number]].

2. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the cryptographic circuit is configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number, __and wherein the mixing circuit applies at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the permutation function or hash function to generate the second entropy value__.

3. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the cryptographic circuit is configured to at least:
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key[[.
wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to at least: implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key]].

4. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator generates the plurality of independent first entropy values [[wherein the hardware source is a ring oscillator, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator]].

5. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator is a single hardware source configured to generate the plurality of independent first entropy values [[wherein the hardware source is a single hardware source, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source]].

6. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein a plurality of independent ring oscillators are configured to generate the plurality of independent first entropy values [[wherein the hardware source is a plurality of independent hardware sources, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware sources]].

7. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the mixing circuit applies at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function [[wherein the function is a permutation function, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function]].

8. (Currently amended) The system of claim 7, wherein the mixing circuit is configured to:
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value [[wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to: divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values; apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value]].

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the mixing circuit applies at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a hash function [[wherein the function is a hash function, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function]].

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the mixing circuit applies at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a bit-mixer [[wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer]].

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the mixing circuit is configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function or hash function to generate the second entropy value [[wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value]].

12. (Cancelled)

13. (Currently amended) A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a ring oscillator;
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function or hash function to generate a second entropy value;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number, wherein the method further comprises implementing countermeasures against phase tracking attacks on the ring oscillator-based entropy source [[receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source; applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value; seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number]].

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number, __and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function or hash function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the permutation function or hash function__.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least:
implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key [[wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least: implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key]].

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator [[wherein the hardware source is a ring oscillator, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator]].

17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator is a single hardware source, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source [[wherein the hardware source is a single hardware source, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source]].

18. (Cancelled)

22. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function or hash function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a bit-mixer [[wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer]].

23. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function or hash function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function or hash function to generate the second entropy value [[wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value]].
